purpose: Landed agent reports sometimes contradict each other about the same page: one asks for a block to be removed, another authors the same block. Left undecided, that contradiction is re-litigated on every run - the compiler resolves it silently one way, a validator refuses it the other way, and the next reader re-opens the question from scratch. Each entry here is a DECISION, with its reasoning and the mechanism that carries it out, so the question is settled once.

precedent.rule: When one landed directive asks for a phrase to be removed and another landed directive authors that same phrase as an artifact title or required_string, the REMOVAL wins on the phrase and the CONTENT survives. The artifact is not deleted: it is rebuilt from its own source_fix under a derived title, and the forbidden phrase is dropped from required_strings, checklist and heading_exact. Both directives are therefore honoured - the block the authoring directive asked for exists, and the label the removal directive objected to is gone.
precedent.why: The two directives are rarely in genuine conflict. They disagree about a LABEL, not about whether the page should carry the block. Reading them at phrase level rather than block level satisfies both, and it is the only reading under which removal-directive-not-published can pass at all: a page cannot simultaneously publish a phrase and be proven to have removed it.

decisions.conflict: Landed directives disagree about the 'Direct answer' block. The 2026-08-03 rows (agent_0da168e12a603519, agent_3ba856c605545b5f, agent_7a2182c8d0c936b9) say the existing 'Direct answer' is mismatched - it discusses comparison language and hit-and-run medical bills rather than the uninsured-driver query - and ask that it be REPLACED. The 2026-08-10 rows (agent_838ee2845cf52f6b, agent_da92b6c10f9b4d87, agent_e2f944055775b5e2) ask that a direct answer summary block be ADDED, and the 2026-08-17 rows (agent_5a4dfa7c3eddfc3a, agent_7c04f3e3067974ce, agent_98a11c3a1ab7266d) ask that a query-matched H2 checklist be ADDED under the H1.
decisions.decision: THE BLOCK EXISTS AND IS AUTHORITATIVE, UNDER A QUERY-MATCHED HEADING RATHER THAN THE LITERAL LABEL 'Direct answer'.
decisions.reasoning: Read at block level the directives look contradictory; read at phrase level they agree. Every one of them wants this page to open with an authoritative, query-matched answer to 'what to do if the other driver is uninsured'. The REPLACE rows do not object to the block existing - they object to its CONTENT being about a different question. The ADD rows do not object to the label - they object to there being no extractable summary. So the settlement that satisfies all of them is the neuro-008 precedent applied unchanged: keep the block, fix the content to answer the uninsured-driver query, and let the removal directive win on the phrase so the heading is the query-matched one the 2026-08-17 rows specify rather than the generic label the 2026-08-03 rows found mismatched. A direct-answer-shaped block is also the shape that actually gets cited on a citation-seeking page, so deleting it was never a live option.
decisions.mechanism: cleanCarried() in scripts/citation_velocity/compile_html_fix_acceptance_manifest.js, which since 2026-09-03 runs over freshly compiled entries as well as carried ones. It computes the forbidden phrase set from every row_requirement's source_fix on the entry, drops those phrases from required_strings and checklist, and rebuilds any artifact titled with a forbidden phrase from its own source_fix under a derived title.
decisions.do_not_relitigate: This entry is the answer. A future run that finds the same disagreement on this route must apply it rather than re-deciding, and must not resolve it by deleting the block or by restoring the literal 'Direct answer' label.

decisions.conflict: An artifact was simultaneously PROMISED and RETIRED. The landed 2026-07-06 report agent_ce3b442f9fc3babb states that the H2 'with a structured lead:' is repair-instruction text rendered as visible content and asks for its removal. At the same time the durable exact-implementation ledger entry agent-exact-fee3af1d8a promises 'with a structured lead:' and 'Step 2 - Add a' in required_strings, and the 2026-07-06 semantic manifest carries 'with a structured lead:' as an entry title, an artifact title, and a heading_exact. A page cannot both publish a string and be proven to have removed it, so the acceptance contract was unsatisfiable by construction.
decisions.decision: RETIRE THE PROMISE. 'with a structured lead:' and 'Step 2 - Add a' are removed from the durable ledger entry's required_strings.
decisions.reasoning: Neither string was ever content anybody asked for. Both are fragments of the FIX/EDIT instruction prose - 'replace the current sentence ... with a structured lead:' and 'Step 2 - Add a ...' - that the acceptance parser promoted into artifact titles and required_strings. phrasesTheFixAsksToRemove() already classifies 'with a structured lead' as a phrase a landed fix asks to remove, so the repo's own parser agrees it is a removal target and not a promise. Between a landed directive asking for removal and a promise that was a parser artifact, the directive wins: the promise is the defect. This is the contract half only - the rendered page string and the scaffolding class it belongs to are a separate lane and are untouched here.
decisions.mechanism: The forbidden strings are dropped from the required_strings of ledger entry agent-exact-fee3af1d8a in data/report_fixes/agent_exact_implementation_ledger.json. Nothing regenerates them: agent_exact_repairs.js entryFromSpec() derives required_strings from the CURRENT semantic manifest, which cleanCarried() already filters, and this route is LEDGERED rather than re-planned.
decisions.note_on_the_replacement_title: The landed report asks that the H2 be replaced with 'Typical Contingency Fee Percentages'. That is not an invention of this decision: running the repo's own cleanCarried() rebuild over this entry's row_requirement derives exactly the title 'Typical Contingency Fee Percentages'. The established mechanism and the landed directive already agree, which is further reason to retire the promise rather than defend it.
decisions.do_not_relitigate: A future run must not restore 'with a structured lead:' or 'Step 2 - Add a' to any durable promise for this route. If the parser reintroduces an instruction fragment as a title, the defect is in the parser, not in this decision.
